issues.legal_issue: A court may not add compensation for future potentiality after determining market value by taking the land’s existing potentiality into account.
material_facts: The acquired land’s market value was determined at Rs. 200 per decimal, with its existing potentiality taken into account.
The reference court added a further 25% to the compensation for future potentiality, and the High Court upheld that increase.
The market value determination itself was not challenged in the appeals.
issues.conclusion: The determination of market value at Rs. 200 per decimal was confirmed, but the additional 25% for future potentiality was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 23(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, market value is assessed as at the date of the Section 4(1) notification and includes the land’s existing or realisable potentiality. Section 24, fifthly and sixthly, prohibits consideration of increases in value likely to arise from the use to which the acquired land will be put or from that use’s effect on other land. V.N. Gajapatiraju v. Revenue Divisional Officer, Visakhapatnam explains that market value includes possibility, not merely realised potential. P. Rama Reddy v. Land Acquisition Officer confirms that building potentiality is included in market value. Land Acquisition Officer, Eluru v. Jasti Rohini states that future development and the prohibited factors in Section 24 must not influence compensation.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: A court is determining compensation for land acquired by the state.
predicates.existing_potentiality_included_in_market: The court determines the land’s market value after taking account of its existing potentiality.
predicates.additional_increase_awarded_for_future_p: The court adds a further increase to compensation on the basis of future potentiality.

issues.definition: When a court determining compensation for acquired land includes existing potentiality in the market value and also adds an increase for future potentiality, the separate increase for future potentiality is disallowed.
